name: The Black Heart Procession
label: Touch and Go
lede: Two Three Mile Pilot members, both freshly dumped, started writing songs for a musical saw and a creaky piano in San Diego. They numbered the first three albums because, as Tobias Nathaniel put it, they hadn't learned that 4 existed.

hero.by: The Black Heart Procession at Touch and Go's 25th anniversary, the Hideout, Chicago, September 2006. Photo: Joel Mills, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A side project with a broken heart
eras.text: Three Mile Pilot had stopped touring, and Pall Jenkins and Tobias Nathaniel had both just come out of relationships. The songs they wrote at Jenkins's house in San Diego were slow, sad and full of odd instruments, and they weren't meant for a record at first.

years.big: "Both me and Tobias had just ended relationships"
q: Both me and Tobias had just ended relationships and were not coping well
years.src: Scaruffi: Black Heart Procession interview · Ondarock interview · Wikipedia: The Black Heart Procession
years.h: Jenkins and Nathaniel start writing during a Three Mile Pilot break
years.p: The other Pilots didn't want to tour, Jenkins told Piero Scaruffi, so the two started a band about sadness. The name: heart for emotion, black for darkness, procession for a sadness shared rather than one man's complaint.
years.xp:
Nathaniel had studied guitar and theory and listened to 20th-century classical music. Jenkins says he took guitar lessons for about a week and liked country and old synthesizers. What came out was built on piano, organ, xylophone and Jenkins's saw.

The first release was A Three Song Recording later that year.

years.src: Bandcamp: 1 · AllMusic: The Black Heart Procession · Ondarock interview · Scaruffi: Black Heart Procession interview
years.h: Eleven songs with "heart" all over them, called 1
years.p: Released on Headhunter, Cargo's imprint. Recorded with Ryan Hadlock at Bear Creek Studio, with [[Mario Rubalcaba|f1c57bba-a668-45fc-b35d-15fac1094cb4]] on drums and Jen Wood singing on one track.
years.xp:
Nearly every title has a heart in it: 'Blue Water, Black Heart', 'Stitched to My Heart', 'A Heart the Size of a Horse'. Jenkins plays guitar, saw, xylophone and synth; Nathaniel piano, organ and bass.

In a 2006 interview with Ondarock, the band remembered 1 as a record made in a single day in the studio; the 2026 reissue's credits give a longer recording window. Jenkins told Scaruffi it was "born almost by accident".

eras.title: Counting to three on Touch and Go
eras.text: Touch and Go picked up the second album, and the band kept the numbers going. By the end of the trilogy the dirges had a following in Europe and the US, and the drummer had left to join Rocket from the Crypt.

years.src: Bandcamp: 2 · Scaruffi: Black Heart Procession interview
years.h: 2 moves the Procession to Touch and Go
years.p: The second chapter, on the Chicago label. Asked later how it came together, Jenkins said they tried to recreate the accident that made the first one.

years.src: AllMusic: The Black Heart Procession
years.h: On the road across the US and Europe with A Minor Forest
years.p: The band tours both continents with San Francisco's A Minor Forest, according to AllMusic.

years.src: Bandcamp: Three · Pitchfork: Six
years.h: Three, spelled out this time, closes the trilogy
years.p: The last numbered album until Six. Pitchfork later remembered the early records for their "creaky drum loops" and empty space.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mario Rubalcaba
years.h: Rubalcaba leaves for Rocket from the Crypt
years.p: The drummer joins San Diego's [[Rocket from the Crypt|e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a]] in September 2000, later playing in [[Hot Snakes|dfa0e21c-ee3e-44da-81d5-58e3c1218a9f]] and founding Earthless.

years.src: Bandcamp: Between the Machines · Tape Op
years.h: Joe Plummer drums on a Suicide Squeeze single in Portland
years.p: Between the Machines b/w After the Ladder is cut by Larry Crane at Jackpot Studios, with [[Joe Plummer|5fd1bd8e-f2b4-4f01-acc0-3423456f06ae]], later of [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]], behind the kit.
years.xp: Crane, who founded Tape Op magazine, met the band this way: recording singles and compilation tracks for them as they came through Portland on tour. He later went to San Diego to interview Jenkins about the studio he'd built.

eras.title: Murder in the tropics, then a real band
eras.text: Amore del Tropico broke the numbering and the formula: a 55-minute noir about lost love and a killing, with more than 30 musicians on some tracks. To make it, Jenkins bought a Studer tape machine and accidentally became a recording engineer.

years.cap: The Black Heart Procession in London, November 2002
years.src: Pitchfork: Amore del Tropico · Tape Op · Ondarock interview · AllMusic: The Black Heart Procession
years.h: Amore del Tropico takes the funeral march south
years.p: A song cycle of love and vengeful murder in an unnamed tropical country, with violinist [[Matt Resovich|f517cfc4-8295-4929-95a1-f46051787df9]] of The Album Leaf now on board. Pitchfork gave it 7.9.
years.xp:
Jenkins recorded it at home after buying a Studer A80 tape machine; he tested the setup on a local band called Teacher's Pet. "I got into gear. It's like an addiction," he told Tape Op. Word got around, other bands asked him to record them, and the home setup grew into a commercial studio, S.D.R.L. (Stereo Disguise Recording Laboratories).

The band told Ondarock some tracks had more than 30 musicians on them, which is why the next album was deliberately simpler.

years.src: Bandcamp: Hearts and Tanks · Wikipedia: The Black Heart Procession
years.h: Locked inside their own studio for 72 hours
years.p: The four-song Hearts and Tanks is tracked in a three-day lock-in at S.D.R.L., with Resovich on accordion. The UK label Shingle Street releases it.

years.src: AllMusic: The Black Heart Procession · Pitchfork: The Spell
years.h: A joint record with Dutch band Solbakken
years.p: In the Fishtank 11, part of the Dutch label Konkurrent's collaboration series. AllMusic hears the band scaling back its usual sinister presentation.

years.cap: The five-piece at the Hi-Dive, Denver
years.src: AllMusic: The Black Heart Procession
years.h: Album Leaf bassist Jimmy LaValle joins
years.p: [[Jimmy LaValle|73a97e9d-e945-4b50-9fd4-e7205eeb77a7]] makes it two Album Leaf members in the line-up.

years.cap: The five-piece Black Heart Procession, c. 2006
q: We had to learn to count with One, Two and Three
years.src: Pitchfork: The Spell · Ondarock interview · Bandcamp: The Spell
yt: Live at the Hi-Dive, Denver, August 10, 2006
years.h: The Spell, the first record by a full five-piece
years.p: Written between Portland and San Diego and recorded at S.D.R.L. Pitchfork's Joe Tangari gave it 8.0 and called it the first album by a fully integrated band.
years.xp:
After Amore, the band told Ondarock, they cut the arrangements back so the songs could be played live by five people. They still went looking for strange sounds, using water tanks and sponges as percussion.

The Not Just Words EP came out on Touch and Go a month earlier, on April 11.

years.src: Wikimedia Commons: Black heart procession.JPG
years.h: Touch and Go's 25th birthday at the Hideout
years.p: The band plays the label's anniversary weekend in Chicago, alongside the label's whole history.

eras.title: Six, a rabbit and a long rest
eras.text: Three Mile Pilot came back to life, and for the first time both of Jenkins and Nathaniel's bands were writing at once. The Procession moved to Temporary Residence, made Six, and then stopped.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Black Heart Procession
years.h: The Waiter Chapters 1–7 on the band's own SDRL label
years.p: A self-released set built around 'The Waiter', the song that opens 1.

years.cap: The Black Heart Procession at the Mohawk, Austin, October 2009
years.src: Pitchfork: Six · Bandcamp: Six
yt: 'Old Kind of Summer', live at KDHX, November 2, 2010
years.h: Six is written alongside a new Three Mile Pilot record
years.p: The first album on Temporary Residence, produced by the band. Pitchfork's Rob Mitchum gave it 6.6 and noted the band is at its peak in October.
years.xp: Mitchum's review opened by lumping the band with costume shops, pumpkin beer and playoff baseball, and thanked whoever schedules Temporary Residence's releases. The label pitched it as the band's most emotionally direct record since Three, on heartbreak, self-destruction and religious allegory.

years.src: Pitchfork: Blood Bunny / Black Rabbit
years.h: Lee "Scratch" Perry remixes the Black Heart Procession
years.p: Blood Bunny / Black Rabbit has three new songs and five remixes, including Perry, Eluvium and Jenkins's own Mr. Tube and the Flying Objects. Pitchfork singled out 'Blank Page' and 'Devotion'.

years.cap: The Black Heart Procession at Dour Festival, Belgium, July 16, 2010
years.src: Wikipedia: The Black Heart Procession · Wikipedia: Three Mile Pilot
years.h: After the EP, the band goes on hiatus
years.p: Jenkins told San Diego CityBeat that after years of touring and traveling they decided to put an end to it for a while.
years.xp: Jenkins kept working: he played optigan, piano and sang on [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]]'s Several Shades of Why (2011), and came back for guitar and vocals on Mascis's Tied to a Star (2014). Three Mile Pilot had already released its comeback, The Inevitable Past Is the Future Forgotten, in September 2010.

eras.title: The procession reforms
eras.text: Two hometown shows turned into a European tour, and the band never quite went away again. A decade on, the old records are back in print on vinyl and the band is playing radio sessions in Seattle.

years.cap: On the European tour: Urban Club, Perugia
years.src: Wikipedia: The Black Heart Procession · Toutpartout
years.h: Two San Diego shows bring the band back
years.p: The Procession reassembles at home, and in December announces 27 European dates for spring 2017.

years.cap: The Black Heart Procession at Magnolia, Milan, March 8, 2017
years.src: Toutpartout · AllMusic: The Black Heart Procession
years.h: Twenty-seven European nights for the debut's anniversary
years.p: The tour, followed by North American dates, backs a deluxe reissue of 1.

years.cap: The Black Heart Procession at Uzeda's 30th, Afrobar, Catania, May 2018
years.src: Rockol
years.h: In Catania for Uzeda's 30th birthday
years.p: The band plays the Sicilian noise band [[Uzeda|9cb56cf1-bd4a-4d59-8ecb-dc412f595dd3]]'s anniversary nights at Afrobar, on a bill with [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]], [[The Ex|ea19687e-8d08-4abe-901e-3135269e4f74]] and [[June of 44|56f3de75-2c88-4054-a1df-65c661f4ee0f]].

years.src: New Noise Magazine · Wikipedia: The Black Heart Procession
yt: The Black Heart Procession, full performance live on KEXP
years.h: A full session on KEXP
years.p: The band plays Seattle's KEXP in early 2025. The station's films include 'Your Church Is Red', 'A Cry for Love' and 'Blue Tears'.

years.p: Between the Machines returns in March, then Hearts and Tanks on September 19.

years.p: Solid Brass reissues the debut with redesigned artwork and the lyrics. Both pressings, 250 red and 350 black, sold out.
